name: C02 Scottish visitor levy returns assistant for B&Bs, guest houses and self-catering (Edinburgh now, Stirling and others next)
buyer: Small accommodation providers in councils that adopt the levy under the Visitor Levy (Scotland) Act 2024: Edinburgh live, Stirling reported from 14 Jun 2027; others in the pipeline (unverified).
trigger: Mandatory registration regardless of turnover or VAT status; quarterly return and payment via the national platform visitorlevy.scot; first Edinburgh return (24 Jul to 30 Sep 2026) due October 2026; records kept 5 years; levy 5% of pre-VAT charge for first 5 nights; booking-date transition rule (bookings paid before 1 Oct 2025 exempt).
existing: Booking/PMS vendors (freetobook, freeonlinebooking, Roommaster) claim levy handling or levy reports; no API or bulk upload for the platform confirmed. Council training covers the platform only, not calculation.
unchecked: Registration deadline, penalty regime (one source: GBP 100 plus 5% of tax due, unconfirmed), whether visitorlevy.scot has bulk upload or API, how many providers are small and not on a PMS, how many councils will adopt next, treatment of OTA bookings, cancellations and refunds.

first_check.duty: Real and in force. Visitor Levy (Scotland) Act 2024, s.26: a return within 30 days of each period end, quarterly by default, with one assessment per premises. Penalties are in ss.47-50 and set by each council; further penalties can apply at 3, 6 and 12 months. Edinburgh's penalty framework (marked partly 'recommended, not implemented') gives a first penalty of 1% of rateable value (indicative £81 to £9,870) for non-residential premises and 10% of annual council tax for residential ones. The claimed 'GBP 100 plus 5%' penalty was not confirmed. Edinburgh: 5% of the accommodation charge for the first 5 nights, stays from 24 Jul 2026, bookings paid on or after 1 Oct 2025, 2% reimbursed to providers, records may be inspected. Glasgow: 5% from 25 Jan 2027. Aberdeen has approved 7% (start date not found). Stirling's earliest start is June 2027 and its final decision was not confirmed. Highland has paused its scheme.
first_check.market: Edinburgh had 3,209 short-term let licences in operation at 31 Dec 2025, and 32,317 across Scotland (Scottish Government statistics). Add Edinburgh B&Bs, guest houses and hotels; no count found. No published figure for providers registered on visitorlevy.scot was found. Glasgow joins in Jan 2027 and Aberdeen later, so roughly 4,000 to 6,000 liable small providers is plausible in the near term (an estimate).
first_check.competitor: Filing and payment go through the free state platform visitorlevy.scot, built by the Improvement Service. Booking and PMS tools found: Hop Software (calculates in night audit, Visitor Levy finance report), Bookster (levy uplift, return reporting 'to be reviewed' before October 2026), freetobook (shows the levy to guests only, no reports or filing), freeonlinebooking and Roommaster (guidance pages). No tool found that prepares the return or submits it to visitorlevy.scot. Airbnb tells Edinburgh hosts they must collect and remit the levy themselves. No bulk upload, agent access or API on the platform was confirmed. Eviivo, Guesty, Lodgify and Little Hotelier: not reached.
first_check.reason: The duty is real. Under the Visitor Levy (Scotland) Act 2024, providers must make a return within 30 days of the end of each period, quarterly by default. Edinburgh's scheme is live: 5% for up to 5 nights, first return due October 2026, filed and paid on the free visitorlevy.scot platform. Glasgow starts 25 Jan 2027. Several booking systems (Hop, Bookster, freetobook, Roommaster) calculate the levy or offer reports, but none was found that files returns, and Bookster says its reporting is still under review. The gap is narrow: turning booking data into a per-property return. The buyers are small hosts with thin margins who get a 2% retention, so willingness to pay is limited. Bulk upload or API on the platform is unverified.

challenge_check.killer: None decisive. Partial overlap: the free visitorlevy.scot platform does the filing, and booking/PMS tools (freeonlinebooking levy reports, Hop finance report, Bookster) do the calculation and reporting. The statutory return is only a levy total per premises per quarter.
challenge_check.reason: No single killer found, but the opening is thin. Filing goes through the free national platform visitorlevy.scot. Under s.26 of the Act, the return is a quarterly figure for each set of premises, so there is little left to "prepare" once the levy is calculated. Booking tools already do the calculation and reporting: freeonlinebooking offers two levy reports you can email to the council, plus refunds and night caps. Hop and Bookster were also found earlier. I found no tool that submits returns to the platform, and no bulk upload or API. More councils are coming, which widens the market: Glasgow approved its levy with a start on 25 Jan 2027, and Stirling plans 2027. The likely buyers are small hosts not on any booking system, a cheap and price-sensitive group. Not checked: provider counts, penalties, and the return form fields.
